chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Muaddib, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, all from Isma'il ibn Mihran, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed the people at Siffin. He praised Allah, extolled Him, and sent blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), then said: 'As for what follows, Allah the Exalted has made for me a right over you by virtue of the guardianship of your affairs, and my status which Allah, Mighty is His mention, has placed me in among you. And you have a right over me equal to what I have over you.'

And the right is the most beautiful of things in description and the most expansive in mutual sharing. It flows for one only if it flows against him, and flows against him only if it flows for him. If it were for one to flow for him and not against him, it would be exclusive to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, apart from His creation, due to His power over His servants and His justice in all that His decrees take. But He made His right upon the servants that they obey Him, and He made their expiation upon Him through good reward, as a grace from Him, an extension of His generosity, and an expansion of what He is worthy of.

Then He made from His rights certain rights He obligated for some people upon others, making them balance each other in their aspects, one obligating the other, and none is obligated except by the other. The greatest of what Allah Blessed and Exalted obligated from those rights is the right of the ruler over the subjects and the right of the subjects over the ruler, an obligation Allah Mighty and Majestic made for each upon the other. He made it the system of their unity, strength for their religion, and establishment of the Sunnah of truth among them. Thus, the subjects are not corrected except by the correction of the rulers, nor are the rulers corrected except by the integrity of the subjects.

So when the subjects fulfill the right of the ruler and the ruler fulfills their right, the right is strengthened between them. The paths of religion are established, the landmarks of justice are balanced, and the Sunnahs flow smoothly. Thus, the era is corrected, life becomes pleasant, hope is placed in the survival of the state, and the ambitions of enemies are frustrated. And if the subjects overpower their ruler and the ruler overpowers the subjects, words differ there, the ambitions of tyranny appear, lawlessness in religion increases, and the landmarks of the Sunnah are abandoned. So they act by desires, effects are neglected, and illnesses of the souls increase. There is no fear of a major penalty being neglected, nor of a great falsehood being established. There, the righteous are humiliated and the wicked are honored, the lands are ruined, and the consequences of Allah Mighty and Majestic become great among the servants.

So come, O people, to cooperating in the obedience of Allah Mighty and Majestic, and establishing His justice, and fulfilling His covenant, and giving Him his due in all of His rights. For the servants are in no greater need than to advise each other in that and to cooperate well upon it. And no one, even if his eagerness for Allah's pleasure is strong and his striving in work is long, reaches the reality of what Allah gave to the rightful owners of the right. But from the obligatory rights of Allah upon the servants is advising Him to the utmost of their ability and cooperating to establish the right among them.

Then, no man, even if his status in the right is great and his virtue in the right is substantial, is independent of being assisted in what Allah Mighty and Majestic has burdened him with of His right. And no man, despite that, whose affairs are humble and whom the eyes overlook, is without being helped and assisted in that. And the people of virtue in the present and the people of great favors are more in need of that. And everyone, in need of Allah Mighty and Majestic, is equal.

Then a man from his army answered him, no one knew who he was, and it is said that he was not seen in his army before that day nor after it. So he stood up and praised Allah Mighty and Majestic beautifully for what He had bestowed upon them and given them of the obligatory right upon them, and acknowledged all that he had mentioned of the changing of states with him and with them. Then he said: 'You are our commander, and we are your subjects. By you, Allah Mighty and Majestic brought us out of humiliation, and by your strengthening, He freed His servants from the yoke. So choose for us and enact your choice, and consult and enact your consultation. For you are the speaking one who is believed, the ruling one who is successful, and the king who is authorized. We do not make disobedience to you permissible in anything, nor do we compare knowledge with your knowledge. Your gravity is great in our eyes, and your virtue is majestic in our souls.'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) answered him, saying: 'Indeed, from the right of one who magnifies the majesty of Allah in his soul and exalts His position in his heart is that everything else seems small to him due to that greatness. And the one most deserving of that is one upon whom the favor of Allah is great and His kindness to him is gentle. For no one's favor of Allah becomes great except that the right of Allah upon him increases in greatness.'

And indeed, of the most foolish states of rulers in the presence of the righteous of people is that they are thought to love pride and their affairs are placed upon arrogance. And I disliked that it should circulate in your opinion that I love flattery and listening to praise. And I am not, by Allah's praise, like that. And if I loved that to be said, I would have abandoned it, lowering myself for Allah, Glory be to Him, from taking what He is more deserving of from greatness and majesty. And perhaps people sweeten praise after affliction. So do not praise me with beautiful praise, for I am taking myself out to Allah and to you from the remainder in rights that I have not finished fulfilling and obligations that must be enacted.

So do not speak to me with what tyrants are spoken to, and do not be cautious with me with what is cautious with the unresponsive, and do not mix with me in flattery, and do not think of me as considering heavy a right said to me, or seeking greatness for myself for what is not suitable for me. For indeed, he who considers heavy the right to be said to him, or justice to be presented to him, the work of both is heavier upon him.

So do not withhold from me a word of right or a consultation of justice. For I am not above making a mistake in myself, nor do I feel secure from that in my action except if Allah suffices for me from myself in what He has more control over than I. For I and you are servants owned by a Lord, there is no lord other than Him, who owns from us what we do not own of ourselves, and brought us out from what we were in to what we were suited for. So He replaced us after guidance with misguidance, and gave us insight after blindness.

So the man who answered him before answered him, saying: 'You are deserving of what I said. By Allah, by Allah, you are above what I said, for His favor upon us is that which is not denied. And Allah Blessed and Exalted has burdened you with our care and appointed you to the governance of our affairs. So you have become our standard by which we are guided and our Imam by whom we follow. And all your command is guidance, and all your word is eloquence. Our eyes have settled with you in life, and our hearts are filled with joy by you, and our intellects are bewildered by the description of what is in you of outstanding virtue.'

And we do not say to you, 'O righteous Imam,' as a purification for you, nor do we exceed the point in praising you. And there is no hidden criticism of your certainty or deceit in your religion in our souls, so we fear that you have become arrogant by the favor of Allah Blessed and Exalted, or that pride has entered you. But we say to you what we said to draw near to Allah Mighty and Majestic by honoring you, and to expand by your excellence, and to give thanks by magnifying your command. So look to yourself and to us, and prefer the command of Allah over yourself and over us. For we are obedient to what you command us, and we submit to the affairs along with that in what benefits us.

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) answered him, saying: 'And I call you to witness against myself before Allah for your knowledge of what I was appointed with from your affairs. And in a little while, the standing before Him will gather me and you, and the questioning of what we were in. Then some of us will testify against the other. So do not testify today against what you will be testifying tomorrow. For Allah Mighty and Majestic does not hide from Him a hidden thing, and what is accepted with Him is only the sincerity of the chests in all of the affairs.'

So the man answered him, and it is said that the man was not seen after this speech of his to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he answered him, and what was in his chest was heavy. He said: 'And weeping cuts off his speech, and the choking of grief breaks his voice, out of magnifying the gravity of his misfortune and loneliness from the occurrence of his calamity. So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then complained to Him of the horror of what he had been cured of from the great danger and the long humiliation in the corruption of his era, and the overturning of his authority, and the cutting off of what was from his state.'

Then he presented the matter to Allah Mighty and Majestic with gratitude upon Him and defending against Him with lamentation and good praise, saying: 'O Lord of the servants, and O Tranquility of the lands! Where does our speech fall from Your grace, and where does our description reach of Your action? And how do we reach the reality of the beauty of Your praise, or count the beauty of Your favor? So how is it, and by you the favors of Allah have flowed upon us, and by your hand the causes of good have connected to us.'

Was he not a refuge for the humiliation of the humiliated, and a brother to the disobedient disbelievers? So by whom, except for the People of your Household, and by you, did Allah Mighty and Majestic bring us out of the horror of those dangers? Or by whom did He relieve us from the floods of distress? And by whom, except by you, did Allah manifest the landmarks of our religion, and correct what was spoiled from our world, until our mention became clear after tyranny, and our eyes settled from the ease of life? For you were our guardian with your effort, and you fulfilled to us all of your promise, and you stood for us upon all of your covenant.

So you were the witness of those who were absent from us, and the successor of the People of the Household for us. And you were the strength of our weak ones, and the wealth of our poor ones, and the pillar of our great ones. It was your justice that gathered us in the affairs, and your patience that expanded for us in the right. So you were for us a companion when we saw you, and a tranquility when we remembered you. So which of the good deeds did you not do, and which of the righteous deeds did you not act upon?

And if it were not for the matter which we fear for you from it reaching, which our effort could change, and our strength could defend against, or if the ransom from it were permissible for you by ourselves and by those we ransom with our souls from our sons, we would have put ourselves and our sons before you, and we would have made this choice, and its danger would have been less than you. And we would have stood with our effort in attempting him who attempted you, and in defending against him who opposed you.

But He is a Sultan who cannot be attempted, and a Might that cannot be opposed, and a Lord who cannot be overcome. So if He bestows upon us your health, and shows mercy to us by your survival, and is compassionate to us by relieving this from your state to a safety of you for us and a survival of you among us, we would narrate to Allah Mighty and Majestic by that a gratitude we magnify, and a remembrance we repeat. And we would divide half of our wealth as charity, and half of our slaves as freedmen, and we would narrate to Him humility in ourselves, and be submissive in all of our affairs.

And if He takes you to the Gardens and makes flow upon you the decree of His path, then His decree is not doubted in you, and his favor is not repelled from you, and our hearts are not different with that that His choice for you is what is with Him over what you were in. But we weep without sin for the might of this Sultan that he should return to humiliation, and for the religion and the world to be consumed. So we do not see for you a successor to whom we complain, nor a counterpart we hope for and establish.
ai.seo_question: What are the mutual rights between the ruler and the subjects according to the sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin at Siffin?
ai.summary: Delivered at Siffin, this sermon articulates the Shia political theology of reciprocal rights (haqq) between the Imam and the community, establishing a symbiotic relationship where societal stability relies on the mutual fulfillment of duties. The Imam explicitly rejects the monarchical arrogance of the Umayyads by distinguishing his leadership from mere power, emphasizing that true authority requires humility and openness to counsel. The narrative concludes with the Imam’s poignant reflection on the inevitability of death and the impending loss of his leadership, highlighting the emotional and spiritual bond with his followers.
